Subject: Post-call: competitive scouting + sanity test sprint for Nimbus Retail

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with Elena (Nimbus Retail):

Summary:
- Use case: product search + re-ranking and SKU enrichment for product detail pages. Low-latency inference at scale (catalog ~1.2M SKUs).
- Primary concerns: hallucination on SKU attributes (brand, materials, dimensions), throughput/cost vs hyperscaler endpoints, and support for long product context (full description + specs).
- Competitors they mentioned evaluating: AWS Bedrock (Titan), Vertex AI endpoints, and Anthropic. They want apples-to-apples quality + cost numbers and a few concrete failure-mode tests.

Asks / next steps (what I promised on the call):
1) Propose a short, high-value sanity test suite we can run in a 3-day sprint (quality + hallucination checks, long-context stress, latency/cost).
2) Run a competitive comparison: Redwood (Redwood-2 small/large quantized variants) vs Bedrock/Vertex/Anthropic on that suite.
3) Provide estimated cost-per-1k tokens and p95 latency numbers (baseline) and a recommended inference config (batching, KV caching, quantization).

Can you each own the pieces below and reply with a quick timeline?
- Monica: design prompts and quality metrics + hallucination definition (50 prompt set + edge cases).
- Sean: test harness for hyperscaler endpoints (latency, cost calc, throughput with batching) and drive the infra.

Elena asked for a tangible mutual action plan by EOW (Friday). I attached the sample catalog they shared on the call — we can sample ~5k SKUs for tests.

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks Rishi — putting together the test plan now. High-level proposal below. I attached the actual prompts file (eval_prompts_v1.txt).

Proposed sanity test suite (priority order):
- A. SKU factualness set (50 prompts): ask explicit attribute questions that should not hallucinate (brand, material, dimensions, color). Evaluate factualness and hallucination incidence.
- B. Long-context retention (20 prompts): include full product description + long spec table; ask to extract or summarize specific fields. p95 latency target here matters.
- C. Instruction-abuse / guardrails (10 prompts): adversarial phrasing intended to elicit hallucinations.
- D. Re-ranking & similarity sanity (30 queries): evaluate retrieval + rerank quality (precision@5, MRR).
- E. Throughput smoke (load test): simple generation/embedding throughput to estimate cost.

Metrics we'll report:
- Hallucination rate (fraction of attribute answers that contradict catalog); enforcement threshold set by Elena = <2% for SKU facts.
- Exact-match accuracy for structured attributes; precision@K for ranking tasks.
- p50/p95 latency for typical payloads (short vs long context).
- Cost-per-1k tokens estimate for each endpoint.

Runner plan / timeline:
- Day 0: sanity prompts and sampling (Monica) — deliver eval_prompts_v1.txt and sample input CSV (done).
- Day 1: run Redwood variants (Monica + infra) across the suite.
- Day 2: run hyperscaler endpoints (Sean) + cost/latency collate.
- Day 3: consolidate results, short slide deck, recommended config.

Edge notes:
- For factual checks we should include SKU aliases and closely-named brands to stress false positives.
- Keep deterministic seeds where possible for sampling.

I'll own the prompt set and initial Redwood runs. Sean — can you confirm access to their Bedrock/Vertex test accounts and estimated cost model?

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Quick operational notes on the hyperscaler comparison and infra setup: 

1) Hyperscaler endpoints to include (explicit):
   - AWS Bedrock (Titan family)
   - Google Vertex AI (PaLM/PaLM2 variants)
   - Anthropic (Claude Instant/Claude 2 if accessible)
   - Redwood: Redwood-2 (standard), Redwood-2-quant (8-bit)

2) Cost / latency approach:
   - I'll capture tokenized consumption per prompt and run short steady-state loads (5 concurrent workers) to get p50/p95 and cost extrapolation per 100k tokens.
   - For hyperscalers I'll use their standard SDKs and sample test accounts (we have credits for Bedrock in the sandbox; need service account for Vertex).

3) Throughput and batching plan:
   - Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 for generation; for embeddings: batch 32/128.
   - Also run KV cache cold vs warm for long-context tempo. Cache hits expected to reduce p95 by ~30% in our runtime.

4) Security & compliance: Elena mentioned they must keep PHI-free and prefer VPC/private endpoints for any PII flow. We should confirm if they will accept our hosted API or require Dedicated/Private in later stages — factor that into cost narrative.

5) Deliverables & links:
   - I'll populate the comparison spreadsheet (comparison_cost_latency.xlsx) in the shared Drive folder and fill an initial cost model.
   - HubSpot deal: HS-983712 (Rishi, please attach the contact record).

Timeline: I can get the hyperscaler runs done by end of Day 2 (2026-01-20) provided I have Vertex service account access today.

- Hard acceptance criteria for the pilot: p95 inference latency for typical product detail extraction <= 150ms (short context), hallucination on SKU facts < 2% across the SKU factualness set, and HTTP success rates > 99.9% for steady-state traffic.
- For cost we primarily care about $/1M requests equivalent (we can convert from tokens). Please show the assumptions used for tokenization.
- We will provide a redacted sample catalog (see attached nimbus_sample_catalog.csv) with product URIs and canonical attributes. Use the attached for the factualness tests.
